To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 25 years between 1970 and1995 were the high‐watermark in clinical oncology and that this is the time when oncology turned into a science from an art
the 25 years between 1970 and mid‐1990 are the high‐waters in the history of cancer research.

(1) cancer is a multifaceted disease that is caused by a combination of factors, (2) the pathomechanisms of the disease are not fully understood but are known to involve genetic and epigenetic changes, (3) the diagnosis of cancer is made by a combination of clinical, radiologic, and histologic methods, and (4) cancer is treated by a combination of surgical and nonsurgical modalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of carcinogenesis and metastasis and the identification of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of human malignancies.
the molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis and the pathomechanisms of the clinical behavior of cancers.
the study of the structure of a protein molecule and its interaction with other molecules in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2 and 1/2 decades of the 1970s and 1980s are the high‐waters of the development of the field of oncology.
the 25 years reviewed (1970–1995) are the high‐waters mark in clinical oncologic research, practice, and teaching.
the 2.5 decades from 1970 to 1995 were the golden age of oncology, and the progress achieved during this period was unprecedented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer is a complex disease, and the care of patients can only be achieved by a multidisciplinary team of specialists.
the 25 years between 1970 and the present are the high‐point in clinical oncology.
the 25‐year period between 1970 and mid‐1995 is the high‐watermark period of clinical oncology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer prevention and advancements in oncology are the key to success in our crusade against cancer.
cancer is a preventable disease.
